meta_description: Denial prevention on a claims lakehouse — initial denial rate down 26% and net collection rate up 4.1 points

blocks.x: Denial prevention on a claims lakehouse — initial denial rate down 26% and net collection rate up 4.1 points

an integrated payer-provider group that was, unusually, both sides of the claim: its hospitals denied its own plan's claims for reasons neither side could see end to end. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline quarter measured the absurdity: 11.8% initial denial rate, EUR — no, USD 34 million net under-collected, and the payer side and provider side reconciling each other's errors by email twice a year.
Denial codes arrived as outcomes, not causes. Registration, coding and authorization failures all looked identical downstream, so prevention was impossible by design.

We built the claims spine both sides read: registration, authorization, coding and adjudication events in one lineage-complete model, denial causes attributed to their originating process, and prevention feeds running to the desks that can actually fix each cause — registration checklists, coding prompts, authorization gates. The denial rate became a managed process variable, not weather.
